content.title: Still Group Anomaly | Expression Shift, Spatial Rupture, Direct Threat
content.summary: Begin with a quiet adult group and one ordinary focal identity. Localize the first anomaly to that person's expression, displace the camera and social space once, hold an empty aftermath, then return the same altered identity from depth until it fills the frame.

quick_start.input_format: quiet adult group, focal identity, and stable space + localized anomaly with three identity anchors preserved + one traceable spatial impact + brief empty aftermath that withholds the focal person + same altered identity approaches along the established depth axis and holds
quick_start.recommended_input: Four adult researchers sit around a steel table. A technician in a moss jacket, clear visor, and orange right-wrist marker changes first; one pressure pulse shifts chairs and camera along the floor line, then the same technician returns from depth behind an opaque visor.
required_anchors: Establish a calm adult group, one focal identity and stable room geometry before any anomaly.
Change one localized feature while preserving at least three identity anchors.
Hold the established environment briefly while withholding the focal adult.
Return the same altered adult from depth and end on increasing proximity rather than a new effect.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Begin with a quiet adult group and one ordinary focal identity. Localize the first anomaly to that person's expression, displace the camera and social space once, hold an empty aftermath, then return the same altered identity from depth until it fills the frame.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Open on one stable social group of clearly adult original characters in a readable room and identify one focal adult through at least three persistent visual anchors. Introduce one localized facial anomaly without changing identity, then escalate exactly once into a traceable displacement of the group, camera or room state. Hold the same environment briefly without the focal adult so the audience reads aftermath and anticipates a return. Reintroduce the same altered adult from an established depth axis and let proximity, not extra effects, drive the final escalation until the face occupies the frame. The reusable mechanism is ordinary group baseline, identity-preserving facial anomaly, one spatial rupture, empty-space consequence gap and same-identity direct approach—not the source people, faces, couch, room, black eyes, hair, exact expressions, motion, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish a calm adult group, one focal identity and stable room geometry before any anomaly.
invariants.ablation_failure: Starting in chaos removes the escalation contrast.

invariants.rule: Change one localized feature while preserving at least three identity anchors.
invariants.purpose: Makes the anomaly belong to the same person.
invariants.ablation_failure: A redesigned face reads as a new subject or continuity error.

invariants.rule: Use one spatially traceable group or camera displacement as the major rupture.
invariants.purpose: Converts private unease into physical consequence.
invariants.ablation_failure: Repeated random shakes become noise rather than progression.

invariants.rule: Hold the established environment briefly while withholding the focal adult.
invariants.purpose: Creates aftermath evidence and a directional question.
invariants.ablation_failure: Immediate reappearance gives no consequence gap.

invariants.rule: Return the same altered adult from depth and end on increasing proximity rather than a new effect.
invariants.purpose: Turns preserved identity into the final threat.
invariants.ablation_failure: A different attacker or unrelated jump cut breaks the causal chain.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source adult group, woman, faces, hair, clothing, couch and exact expressions
the source domestic room, furniture, walls, floor, openings and exact staging
the source solid black eyes, possession appearance and hair transformation
the source camera displacement, group motion, low angles, approach and terminal close-up
the source creator identity, Seedance 2.5 wording and 20-second timing
